`SCRIPT_START_FAILED` means the runner proved the command did not start. After restoring an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, Resume can retry the pinned definition. If the command, arguments or working-directory configuration must change, publish the corrected definition and start a fresh run. Neither Resume nor Replay applies that definition change: both retain the failed run's pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](07-troubleshooting.md#windows-batch-commands). `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN` means the previous attempt may already have produced its effect before its disposition was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed; **Recover script** opens an explicit choice: **Resume** runs it again in this run, **Replay** starts a new run from the failed node, **Cancel** leaves it failed. Both retry choices may repeat the effect. `failure.script` identifies the visit, dispatch, execution state and any known exit code. Completed nonzero exits still use `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`.

For `SCRIPT_OUTCOME_UNCERTAIN`, the previous script attempt may already have produced its effect before its result was recorded. Recovery leaves it failed. Inspect the external system, then choose **Recover script**: **Resume** runs it again in the same run; **Replay** runs it in a new run from the failed node; **Cancel** leaves the run failed. Either retry may repeat the effect. `SCRIPT_START_FAILED` instead means the runner proved the command did not start. Restore an external prerequisite, such as a missing executable, then explicitly Resume. To change the command, arguments or working-directory configuration, publish the corrected definition and start a fresh run; neither Resume nor Replay applies the change because both keep the pinned version. See [Windows batch commands](#windows-batch-commands). Nonzero completed exits retain `SCRIPT_EXIT_CODE`. The failure's `script` fields identify the visit, dispatch, state and known exit code.

The correction changes exactly `docs/04-node-catalog.md`, `docs/guide/03-run-and-observe.md` and `docs/guide/07-troubleshooting.md`. Restoring an external prerequisite can permit ordinary Resume. Changing the command, arguments or working-directory configuration requires a corrected published definition and a fresh run; Resume and Replay retain the old pinned version. The Windows batch subsection follows the general symptom table and retains its anchor.

The response is HTTP 202 with a `run` object. Save `run.id`; execution continues in the background. Specify `triggerNodeId` when selecting among several triggers. `input` must match the manual trigger's schema, or the request fails with 400 `INVALID_INPUT`. `return` adds channels to the exit's channels. Optional `versionId` pins a particular version. A loop with no published version returns 404 `LOOP_NOT_FOUND`, and a draft `versionId` without `allowDraft` returns 409 `VERSION_NOT_PUBLISHED`. To try an unpublished draft, supply the draft's `versionId` (from `GET /loops/{id}`) and set `allowDraft` true. The run answers with a new `versionId`: a snapshot of the draft taken at start, which later draft edits never change. The UI runs published versions.

| Starting a run returns 404 `LOOP_NOT_FOUND` or 409 `VERSION_NOT_PUBLISHED`                                                                                     | Wrong loop ID, no published version, or a draft version without `allowDraft`.                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Check the ID, publish, or pass `allowDraft` true with the draft's `versionId`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
